name: Tarshish
overview: Tarshish is a male figure identified as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media, as noted in Esther 1:14. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him. His role as a prince highlights his position of authority within the Persian and Median empire during the events described in the book of Esther.
namesAndTitles: The name Tarshish is a proper name and may mean 'yellow jasper,' 'greedy one,' or relate to a 'foundry' or 'refinery,' though these meanings are not definitively confirmed. The name was not given by God but is significant as it appears in the biblical record in Esther 1:14.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Tarshish beyond his identification as one of the princes of Persia and Media. There are no additional relationships listed or implied in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tarshish's significance lies in his role as one of the seven princes who served under King Ahasuerus in the Persian empire. This position places him among the highest-ranking officials during the time Esther's story unfolds, indicating his involvement in the governance and administration of the kingdom. His mention underscores the structured leadership within Persia and Media at that time.
